query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Combining CALPHAD thermodynamic modelling with targeted experiments will predict the high-temperature behaviour of the alloy more reliably than trial-and-error testing.
generation.intervention: A CALPHAD-guided design and validation workflow.
generation.structural_mediator: Predicted phase fractions and stability ranges.
generation.mechanism: Thermodynamic databases capture the phase equilibria that govern high-temperature behaviour.
generation.predicted_outcome: Better agreement between predicted and measured phases than empirical screening.
generation.boundary: Holds where the thermodynamic database is reliable.

falsification_experiment.design: Compare treated and reference samples under the stated conditions.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: No improvement over the baseline rejects it.
